scope: Targeted primary-paper screen, not an exhaustive systematic review. All results are reported by authors; no causal estimate reproduced in this workstream.

papers.title: Provisional COVID-19 infrastructure induces large, rapid increases in cycling
papers.design: Generalized difference in differences; city treatment intensity; counter, city-week and country-day effects in preferred specification.
papers.assignment: Authors argue timing is as good as random from administrative/contractor schedules; not a randomized trial.
papers.moving_lane_conversion: Mixed/uncertified: underlying policy data cannot systematically distinguish implementation types.
papers.reported_result: Abstract: 11–48% increase in cycling across specifications; not an all-mode result.
papers.replication_status: Archive acquired and checksum verified, but advertised panel is a Git LFS pointer. Linked repository/object returned 404. No model reproduced.
limits: Cycling-only counts do not establish mode substitution or total persons/time.
COVID and dense-city context constrain transport.
Berlin overlaps this sample; do not double-count as independent evidence.
papers.evidence_read: Full primary article and archived code/metadata
papers.registry_role: Mechanism evidence; not certified moving-lane conversion effect

papers.title: The Causal Effect of Cycling Infrastructure on Traffic and Accidents: Evidence from Pop-Up Bike Lanes in Berlin
papers.version: June 2022 PDF; later SSRN version exists and must not be silently combined.
papers.observed_sample: 23 treated sensors in six streets versus 192 controls; 2019–2020 hourly traffic data, selected weekday/daytime coverage.
papers.design: Difference-in-differences; eligible multi-lane roads and timing argued conditionally quasi-random; nearby controls excluded.
papers.assignment: Eligibility and contractor availability arguments, not random assignment.
papers.moving_lane_conversion: Yes: motor moving lanes replaced by cycle lanes.
papers.reported_result: Adjusted Table 1: speed −4.123 km/h; log speed −0.122; log volume −0.0054 (not statistically significant).
papers.replication_status: Official raw sensor files acquired separately by Europe workstream; no verified processed replication package found. Published estimates not reproduced.
limits: Paper averages volume and speed across lanes: full cross-section flow must be independently reconstructed.
Official metadata identifies cycle-lane detector deinstallations; post-treatment sensor completeness requires audit.
Spot speed is not journey time; no aligned bicycle/transit/person outcome.
papers.evidence_read: Primary June PDF; Europe agent separately audits official data.
papers.registry_role: Direct conversion case with partial outcomes; measurement gate remains

papers.title: Heterogeneous impacts of protected bike lanes on bikeshare behavior across demographic groups in New York
papers.authors: Marcel Moran; Malik Salman; Takahiro Yabe
papers.observed_sample: 72 million selected Citi Bike trips; source data span 2013–2024.
papers.design: Propensity score matching plus two-way fixed-effects difference in differences at station-month level; protected and painted treatment categories.
papers.assignment: Observational installation; conditional parallel trends required.
papers.moving_lane_conversion: Not established: lane type is classified, but loss of motor moving lanes is a separate eligibility question.
papers.reported_result: Authors report 379 additional rides per station-month after protected-lane installation (p<0.001); painted-lane causal effect not detected.
papers.replication_status: Full primary article acquired. Availability statement links public raw Citi Bike and NYC bike-lane data; no processed panel or code repository identified in article. No model reproduced.
limits: Bike-share starts are not all bicycle crossings or total mobility.
Matching observed neighborhood characteristics does not establish exogenous placement.
Staggered TWFE requires heterogeneous-effect and spillover audit.
papers.evidence_read: Full publisher HTML acquired after web-reader redirect; methods and availability reviewed.
papers.registry_role: Local mechanism comparator; not independent all-mode confirmation

papers.title: Cycling infrastructure and its co-benefits: Evidence from a longitudinal natural experiment
papers.authors: Jérôme Laviolette; Zahra Zarabi; Kevin Manaugh; Owen Waygood
papers.observed_sample: 2.5 km protected lanes; longitudinal intervention/control surveys in 2023 and 2024.
papers.design: Before/after difference in differences of survey mode use and perceptions.
papers.moving_lane_conversion: Unverified; abstract notes on-street parking removal as possible mechanism.
papers.reported_result: Driving share decreased significantly; cycling and walking share increases were not significant.
papers.replication_status: No downloadable analysis panel acquired; abstract only verified.
limits: No verified moving-lane loss.
Shares are not person-throughput levels or complete journey time.
Sample size, attrition, parallel trends and data access require full-text review before causal weighting.
papers.evidence_read: Publisher abstract and author institutional bibliographic record.

papers.title: Does new bicycle infrastructure result in new or rerouted bicyclists? A longitudinal GPS study in Oslo
papers.observed_sample: 113 GPS-app participants; published exposed/quasi-control comparison groups include 39 and 47 people.
papers.design: Longitudinal GPS natural experiment around a contraflow cycle lane.
papers.reported_result: Treated-route cycling increased while parallel-route cycling declined; cycling mode-share change was not statistically significant.
limits: Small selected app panel.
Route substitution warns against equating a treated counter increase with net new cyclists.
Not an all-mode throughput estimate.
papers.registry_role: Design lesson: separate rerouting from mode shift

papers.title: All ages and abilities cycling infrastructure, cycling activity, and perceived safety: Findings from a natural experiment study in three mid-sized Canadian cities
papers.geography: Victoria, with Kelowna and Halifax comparisons
papers.observed_sample: 33 km AAA network; repeated population surveys in 2016, 2019 and 2021, roughly 1000 per city-wave.
papers.design: City/distance/time comparison; distance within 500m as exposure.
papers.moving_lane_conversion: Mixed network; not certified moving-lane conversions.
papers.reported_result: No statistically different cycling change for proximity comparison; control-city investment and COVID complicate inference.
papers.replication_status: Primary indexed article says authors cannot share data.
limits: Control contamination.
COVID and delayed completion.
No vehicle/transit throughput or full journey outcome.
papers.evidence_read: Primary publisher indexed abstract and availability excerpt.
papers.registry_role: Include null/ambiguous mechanism evidence to avoid positive-case selection

papers.title: Have paved trails and protected bike lanes led to more bicycling in Atlanta? A generalized synthetic-control analysis
papers.observed_sample: Five infrastructure groups; monthly Strava 2016-10 to 2018-09 calibrated using 15 physical counters.
papers.design: Generalized synthetic control; treatment areas and counter-based app-usage adjustment.
papers.moving_lane_conversion: Mixed off-street trails and protected bike lanes; not certified conversion subset.
papers.reported_result: Joint ratio 1.10 (95% CI 0.99–1.18) for narrower treatment definition; effects differ by project.
limits: App sample and calibration may not represent all trips.
Counter calibration does not identify car/transit substitution.
Bicycle-distance is a distinct outcome from crossings, trips, or time.
papers.evidence_read: Primary full-text indexed methods/results; direct open encountered browser challenge.
papers.registry_role: Method candidate: app calibration and heterogeneous synthetic controls
